explanation: A parallel-plate capacitor stores charge by separating + and - on two plates a distance d apart. Its capacitance C = epsilon0·A/d says how many coulombs it holds per volt: bigger plate area A gives more room for charge (C grows), while a wider gap d weakens the field's grip and LOWERS C. Slide A and watch the plates grow taller; slide d and watch the gap — and the live pF readout — respond exactly as the formula predicts.
bullets: C measures charge stored per volt: Q = C·V, in farads (here picofarads).
More plate area A raises C; a larger gap d lowers C (C is inversely proportional to d).
epsilon0 = 8.85e-12 F/m is the permittivity of free space; a dielectric would multiply C up.
